arxiv-2012-01515.title: The perturbative CFT optical theorem and high-energy string scattering in AdS at one loop
arxiv-2012-01515.creator: António Antunes † , Miguel S. Costa † , Tobias Hansen ◇ , Aaditya Salgarkar † , Sourav Sarkar †
arxiv-2012-01515.description: Abstract We derive an optical theorem for perturbative CFTs which computes the double discontinuity of conformal correlators from the single discontinuities of lower order correlators, in analogy with the optical theorem for flat space scattering amplitudes. The theorem takes a purely multiplicative form in the CFT impact parameter representation used to describe high-energy scattering in the dual AdS theory.

arxiv-2201-05225.creator: Mason del Rosario and Zhi Ding
arxiv-2201-05225.description: Abstract Wireless links using massive MIMO transceivers are vital for next generation wireless communications networks networks. Precoding in Massive MIMO transmission requires accurate downlink channel state information (CSI). Many recent works have effectively applied deep learning (DL) to jointly train UE-side compression networks for delay domain CSI and a BS-side decoding scheme.

arxiv-2206-00816.title: Quintet formation and exchange fluctuations: The role of stochastic resonance in singlet fission
arxiv-2206-00816.creator: Miles I. Collins, Francesco Campaioli, Murad J. Y. Tayebjee, Jared H. Cole, Dane R. McCamey
arxiv-2206-00816.description: Abstract Singlet fission describes the spin-conserving production of two triplet excitons from one singlet exciton. The existence of a spin-2 (quintet) triplet-pair state as a product of singlet fission is well established in the literature, and control of quintet formation is an important step towards applying singlet fission in photovoltaics and quantum information.

arxiv-2404-01965.title: Towards Leveraging AutoML for Sustainable Deep Learning: A Multi-Objective HPO Approach on Deep Shift Neural Networks
arxiv-2404-01965.creator: Leona Hennig, Tanja Tornede, Marius Lindauer
arxiv-2404-01965.description: Abstract Deep Learning (DL) has advanced various fields by extracting complex patterns from large datasets. However, the computational demands of DL models pose environmental and resource challenges. Deep shift neural networks (DSNNs) offer a solution by leveraging shift operations to reduce computational complexity at inference.

arxiv-2602-06551.title: AB Aur, a Rosetta stone for studies of planet formation (IV): C/O estimates from CS and SO interferometric observations.

arxiv-2602-06551.description: Abstract Context. Protoplanetary disks are the birthplace of planets. As such, they set the initial chemical abundances available for planetary atmosphere formation. Thus, studying elemental abundances, molecular compositions, and abundance ratios in protoplanetary disks is key to linking planetary atmospheres to their formation sites. Aims.

pmc-10500262.title: Whole-genome detection using multivalent DNA-coated colloids
pmc-10500262.creator: Peicheng Xu, Ting Cao, Qihui Fan, Xiaochen Wang, Fangfu Ye, Erika Eiser
pmc-10500262.description: SignificanceThere is a great need for easy tests identifying infection-causing bacteria. Identifying bacterial DNA using the polymerase chain reaction may be problematic in low-tech environments. Here we present and test a method to identify whole bacterial genomes without using DNA amplification. Our experiments validate an approach proposed in simulations (PNAS 117, 8719–8726 (2020)).

pmc-10539680.title: Joint modeling of forced vital capacity measures with time to onset of polycythemia among chronic obstructive pulmonary outpatients follows‐up: A case of University of Gondar Referral Hospital

pmc-10539680.description: Background and AimsChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) causes airflow obstruction and respiratory problems. pmc-10651751.title: The effects of trauma on feedback processing: an MEG study
pmc-10651751.creator: Abdulrahman S. Sawalma, Christian M. Kiefer, Frank Boers, N. Jon Shah, Nibal Khudeish, Irene Neuner, Mohammad M. Herzallah, Jürgen Dammers
pmc-10651751.description: The cognitive impact of psychological trauma can manifest as a range of post-traumatic stress symptoms that are often attributed to impairments in learning from positive and negative outcomes, aka reinforcement learning. Research on the impact of trauma on reinforcement learning has mainly been inconclusive.

pmc-11378125.title: Digoxin treatment does not reinduce radioiodine uptake in radioiodine refractory non-medullary thyroid carcinoma
pmc-11378125.creator: Pepijn van Houten, James Nagarajah, Janneke E W Walraven, Martin Jaeger, Adriana C H van Engen-van Grunsven, Johannes W Smit, Romana T Netea-Maier
pmc-11378125.description: ObjectivePatients with non-medullary thyroid carcinoma (NMTC) that are refractory to radioactive iodine (RAI) have a poor prognosis. Strategies for restoring the ability to take up iodine, so-called redifferentiation, are promising but not suitable for all patients. Preclinical studies, in human cell lines just as in a murine model, have shown that the cardiac glycoside digoxin restored RAI uptake.

pmc-12609587.title: A Three-Decade Analysis of Ischemic Stroke in India: Mortality, Morbidity, and Risk Factors Using the Global Burden of Diseases Study from 1990 to 2019
pmc-12609587.creator: Aditya D. Goyal, Avi A. Gajjar, Najib Muhammad, Albert Q. Wu, Hanish Polavarapu, Oliver Tang, Mohamed M. Salem, Ethan D. Paliwoda, Nithin Gupta, Jagroop Doad, Brian T. Jankowitz, Visish M. Srinivasan, Jan-Karl Burkhardt
pmc-12609587.description: Background/Objectives: India has experienced a sharp increase in stroke burden over the last half-century. The diverse geographical conditions and developing health infrastructure warrant an investigation into changes in mortality and morbidity due to ischemic stroke. This research aims to estimate the impact of attributable risk factors, providing comprehensive insights into the temporal trends of ischemic stroke in India.
